title: Binary Search
source: canonical Binary Search concept; description, examples, and tests re-authored
description: The input is an array of integers sorted in ascending order and a target value. Return the index of target in the array, or -1 when it never appears. Every value in the array is distinct, so at most one index matches.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order
every value in nums is distinct

examples.explanation: The value 16 sits at index 4 of the sorted array.
Neither 3 nor 7 equals 5, so the target is absent.

hints: The sorted order lets one comparison throw away half of the remaining candidates.
Keep two indices bounding the range still worth searching, and inspect only its middle value.
While lo <= hi: mid = (lo + hi) // 2. Equal returns mid, too small moves lo to mid + 1, too large moves hi to mid - 1. Return -1 after the loop.
solution: Halve the search range every step: compare the middle value with the target and discard the half that cannot hold it. O(log n) time, O(1) space.
failureHint: hidden tests include a single value, targets at both ends, and absent targets

visible.failNote: return the index, not the value
